testResults.result: 42 cases: imports, dunder access, dangerous calls, wall-clock, sleeping, networking, subprocess, concurrency, async syntax, and nested-import evasion all rejected with stable error kinds

testResults.result: fresh-subprocess execution with wall-clock kill (tested at 3 seconds against idle and busy infinite loops), 64 MiB request cap, protocol tampering rejected, Windows spawn verified; worker killed and reaped on timeout with a TIMEOUT error carrying the script hash

testResults.name: sandbox-parity-and-determinism
testResults.command: uv run --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/harness/screening/test_parity.py
testResults.result: Deterministic scripts produce exact-equality results in the sandbox vs the in-process reference executor, and repeated sandbox runs are deterministic

testResults.name: golden-and-cold-start
testResults.command: uv run --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/harness/screening/test_golden.py tests/harness/screening/test_cold_start.py
testResults.result: Legitimate script using facts and host-computed sma_5 series produces hand-computed per-symbol booleans; worker cold start measured at mean 111 ms worst 113 ms over three runs, five-symbol batch through one worker at 109 ms

limitations: No OS-level memory cap is available in the Windows stdlib sandbox; the wall-clock kill plus 64 MiB request cap plus the locked import surface are the production mitigations and scripts are trusted-author artifacts by policy
A killed batch loses all its work by design (never partial results)
Scripts see only their own symbol's context; cross-sectional surfaces are deferred
